Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

policy noun

also line, course of action, principle, it’s my policy

classical

Cic. Fam. 1.8.3
Sall. Cat. 56.5: aliēnum suīs ratiōnibus, against his policy (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 148, 362

ratiō, ratiōnis f.

noun, third declension

a policy, a line of conduct

Lewis & Short: course, conduct, procedure, plan; in the plural, one’s interests and policy.

Examples

  • haec ego ad tē ob eam causam maximē scrībō, ut jam dē tuā quoque ratiōne meditēre

    my main reason for writing this is that you should now think about your own policy tooCic. Fam. 1.8.3

  • Dē suā ratiōne interrogātus, ambiguus fit.

    When asked about his own policy, he becomes evasive.Traupman 148

Other words

  • cōnsilium, cōnsiliī n. — a plan, a measure decided on

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Caes. BG 1.21: quid suī cōnsiliī sit, ostendit (Lewis & Short)

  • īnstitūtum, īnstitūtī n. — a practice, a rule one keeps

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 4.18: oblītum cōnsuētūdinis et īnstitūtī meī (Lewis & Short)

    For “it’s my policy”: what one habitually does.

See also government, political, system.

SourcesLewis & Short: ratio · Lewis & Short: consilium · Lewis & Short: institutum
